before.text:
We study properties of zeros of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s).
Levinson and Montgomery [8] achieved several important theorems for the behav-
ior of zeros of ζ (m) (s) (m = 1, 2, 3, · · · ). If we assume the Riemann hypothesis,
ζ ′ (s) has no non-real zero in Re s < 21 and ζ (m) (s) (m > 1) has at most ﬁnitely
many zeros in Re s < 12 . Unconditionally, we are able to deduce the following
quantitative results by similar methods in [8].

unit_result_entry.title: Hyperbolic-sine trial mollifier and balancing-parameter optimization
unit_result_entry.why_material: Relaxes the polynomial infimum to a continuous hyperbolic-sine trial function, balances two integral contributions by choosing a parameter, and estimates the Q_k integrals to obtain a large-order constant bound.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This is a constructive variational step, not merely routine algebra, because the trial family and balancing choice drive the asymptotic coefficient.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent: the trial function, lambda choice, integral evaluations, and big-O terms are extraction-degraded and require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Differential-polynomial proxy for J_k and import of the mollified mean square
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Constructs V_k using Q_k(x)=(1-x)^k, replaces the J_k mean square asymptotically by the V_k mean square through chi asymptotics and integration by parts, then invokes Conrey's theorem.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Conversion of the optimized mean-square constant into derivative-zero abundance
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Combines the optimized constant with the zero-count inequality and the total derivative-zero count to obtain the stated positive proportion and its large-order behavior.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Littlewood and Jensen reduce a derivative-zero count to a mollified J_k mean square; a differential-polynomial proxy places it under Conrey's theorem; a trial mollifier and balancing optimization then yield a positive-proportion result.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The result is conditional on the cited mean-square theorem, and the extracted optimization formulas require scan verification.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Mollified mean-square route to derivative-zero abundance
